text:
linda: Heads up — noticed some services stopped receiving secret rotations after the TF apply last night. Noticed ExternalSecrets lastSyncTime unchanged. Can someone quick-check the TF diff?

mike: saw that too. Repro steps: kubectl get externalsecret -n payments stripe-secret -o yaml shows annotation not present. Looks like we renamed the annotation key in the module.

mike: excerpt from the TF change in the PR:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "externalsecret" {
  manifest = yamlencode({
    apiVersion = "kubernetes-client.io/v1"
    kind = "ExternalSecret"
    metadata = {
      name = var.name
      annotations = {
        # old key -> new key rename happened here
        "external-secrets.io/refresh" = var.refreshSchedule
      }
    }
  })
}
```

linda: the live cluster had "externalsecrets.kubernetes.io/refresh" previously (note the plural upstream integration). TF looks to be writing the singular form.

tom: ah that explains it — the external-secrets controller only watches the old annotation name in the version we're running in prod; upstream changed in newer controller releases. Module bump introduced the new key.

linda: quick mitigation options?

mike: two quick options: 1) patch existing ExternalSecret resources to include the old annotation as well so controller picks them up, or 2) revert the module change in TF and reapply. First is fastest.

tom: I can push a one-off kubectl patch to add the old annotation for affected namespaces. Example: 
```bash
kubectl -n payments patch externalsecret stripe-secret --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"externalsecrets.kubernetes.io/refresh":"now"}}}'
```

oncall: if we patch, do we also need to update the reconciliation controller to avoid flapping? Which controller version is in prod?

mike: prod is on external-secrets v0.5.1 which still expects the plural key. Newer versions accept the new key. We should avoid controller changes during business hours.

ci-bot: deploybot: created rollback branch revert/module-annotation-rename, CI queued (PR #4821).

linda: ok plan: tom patches affected ES in payments and billing now, mike will run a one-off script to enumerate clusters/namespaces to patch any missing annotations, I'll open a PR to add backwards-compatible annotation mapping in the TF module (write both keys) and tag mike + eng-oncall for review.

mike: script snippet I used locally: 
```bash
for ns in payments billing; do
  kubectl -n $ns get externalsecret -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["external-secrets.io/refresh"] and (.metadata.annotations["externalsecrets.kubernetes.io/refresh"] | not)) | .metadata.name' | xargs -r -n1 -I{} kubectl -n $ns patch externalsecret {} --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"externalsecrets.kubernetes.io/refresh":"now"}}}'
done
```

tom: patched payments, stripe-secret shows lastSyncTime updated after controller picked it up. :thumbsup:

linda: thanks — opening PR now and adding a short runbook step for post-deploy verification. Assigning mike to review. Will monitor rotation metrics for the next hour.

oncall: ping me if anything else pops.

mike: will follow up with a cleanup task to remove the temporary patch once controller is upgraded to one that supports the new key.

linda: recording this in the infra runbook under ExternalSecrets -> annotation compatibility.

ci-bot: PR #4821 opened by linda: https://git.company/repos/infra/pulls/4821

linda: resolved for now, marking this thread closed unless we see more failures. Thanks all.
